principles.title: Readable, maintainable code
principles.description: Code is read far more often than it is written. Clear names, simple structure, and honest comments make it easier to change later.

principles.title: The right tool for the problem
principles.description: Languages, frameworks, and dependencies are chosen deliberately, based on the problem rather than habit or trend.

principles.title: Small, reviewable changes
principles.description: Work moves forward in small steps with a clear history in version control, which makes problems easier to find and fix.

principles.title: Accessible and fast by default
principles.description: Accessibility and performance are built in from the start instead of being added at the end.

principles.title: Security as a habit
principles.description: Secrets stay out of code, dependencies stay minimal and current, and access is limited to what is actually needed.

principles.title: Documentation that explains why
principles.description: Good documentation records decisions and trade-offs, not just usage.
